items.title: Personal experience drives Fadhlina's push for better caregiver support for working mothers
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said her personal experiences of child abuse and loss had strengthened her commitment to improving caregiver support for working mothers. Fadhlina said her second child was abused by a caregiver who hit the child on the legs while she was working as a lawyer with a demanding schedule. Fadhlina, who has six children, said three of them had been placed under the care of caregivers, adding that finding suitable childcare was a major challenge for working mothers.

items.title: 27 illegal snares destroyed in Selangor, Perak wildlife operation
items.summary: Perhilitan director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said the 27 snares comprised spring traps, wire loop snares and nylon loop snares. "The type and size of snares used generally depend on the species of wildlife being targeted. "Spring traps are commonly used to target wild boar, while wire and nylon loop snares can be used to target larger or smaller wildlife, depending on the diameter of the wire or rope and the size of the spring mechanism used," he said in a statement today.

items.title: MACC detains company owner for allegedly soliciting RM30,000 to secure defence‑sector financing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Kuala Lumpur has arrested an owner of a consulting, management and business company on suspicion of soliciting and accepting bribes of about RM30,000 in return for obtaining grants and loans under the Bumiputera entrepreneur financial financing scheme for two companies related to armaments and defence. According to sources, the woman, in her 60s, was arrested at about 6.45pm on Thursday around Kuala Lumpur. Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohamad Zakkuan Talib when contacted confirmed the arrest and the case is being investigated under Section 16(a) (A) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: 11 detained to assist probe into group attack in Ipoh
items.summary: Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the 26-year-old victim was approached by five men travelling in two cars at about 10.30am, who then chased and assaulted him. Mohd Alwi said members of the public later came to the victim's aid before taking him to hospital for treatment. Mohd Alwi said all those arrested, aged between 22 and 41, had previous criminal records involving drug offences and violent crimes.

items.title: Serian tops very unhealthy API readings as six Sarawak areas exceed 200
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — A total of six areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at very unhealthy levels as of 1pm today with Serian recording the highest reading of 287. Deputy Director-General (Development) of the Department of Environment (DOE) Azuri Azizah Saedon said five other areas in the state that recorded very unhealthy readings were Kuching (267), Sri Aman (251), Samarahan (242), Samalaju (202) and Bintulu (201). She said 25 areas recorded API readings at unhealthy levels involving Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Johor, Pahang, Sabah, Labuan, Sarawak and Selangor, in addition to 26 areas recording moderate air quality status and 11 areas at good levels.

items.title: From janitor to senior lecturer: UM academic turns experience into PhD research
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: From collecting rubbish as a janitor to becoming a senior lecturer at Universiti Malaya, Dr Nurul Asmaa Akmal Md Din has turned years of hard work into an academic career. Nurul Asmaa, 30, drew on her experience in waste management for her doctoral research. She said the job proved valuable rather than a setback, with her experience in waste management later forming the basis of her PhD research.

items.title: Pas-Umno ummah unity must move beyond resolutions, says Tuan Ibrahim
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The ummah unity between Pas and Umno, which was unanimously endorsed at the Islamist party's muktamar, must be translated into action. Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said support for the unity would usually be tested when negotiations on seat allocations for the general election begin. "The muktamar has unanimously approved the strengthening of ummah unity, particularly with many people talking about unity or cooperation between Pas and Umno.

items.title: In Nepal for eight days, Malaysian wife presses on with search for missing special‑operations firefighter
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Hani Othman, who has been in Nepal for eight days to follow the developments in the search for her missing Special Airborne Fire and Rescue Team (PASKUB) officer husband, today joined a mission to distribute humanitarian aid to disaster victims in the country, while hoping to find any clues as to her husband. Hani, who is currently on her way from Nuwakot to Betrawati with the local non-governmental organisations (NGO) Samundra Nepal NGO and Himalayan Leaders, said that the area they are heading to is not the last location where her husband’s vehicle was detected, but she still hopes that the journey will yield clues. “The area of my husband’s last point is further up.

items.title: Haze-linked health problems on the rise, asthma cases jump eightfold
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Asthma, bronchitis, acute respiratory tract infections (URTI) and conjunctivitis are among the health problems reported to have increased amid the haze currently blanketing the country. Public health medicine specialist Datuk Dr Zainal Ariffin Omar said the increase was linked to inflammation of the respiratory tract caused by haze. "Conjunctivitis can also occur as haze particles directly irritate the eyes," he said.

items.title: Malaysia sends families’ DNA samples to Nepal to help identify 55 missing Malaysians, says Tok Mat
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 5 — All DNA samples from the next-of-kin of 55 Malaysians still unaccounted for following floods and landslides in Nepal have been obtained, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. He said the samples would be sent to Nepal for the authorities there to conduct DNA matching, a process expected to take some time given the large number of victims involved. Mohamad said Malaysia was also prepared to send experts from the Department of Chemistry to assist the Nepalese authorities with the DNA matching process, if required.

items.title: Transform old assets to create new economic value, says Johari
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Old assets that are no longer being utilised optimally should be transformed to create new economic value, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said. The Investment, Trade and Industry Minister said investors' willingness to take risks, backed by capital, creativity and sound management, could revitalise old assets while benefiting the surrounding business ecosystem. "Equipped with vision, capital, creativity and sound management, such assets can be given a second life and, in turn, create new economic value," he said.

items.title: Human-wildlife conflict complaints hit 76,000, losses top RM58.7mil
items.summary: KUALA BERANG: Complaints over human-wildlife conflicts nationwide, particularly those involving elephants, have reached 76,000 since 2021, with property and crop damage exceeding RM58.7 million. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the rising number of complaints was a cause for concern. He said the increase in conflicts was largely due to large-scale land clearing for agriculture and development, which destroyed and encroached on elephants' traditional roaming areas.

items.title: Chew Jetty heritage site unaffected by blaze, Penang govt to help owners of five destroyed premises, says CM
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 5 — The historic Chew Jetty here was unaffected by a fire that broke out about 20 metres away and destroyed five business premises early this morning, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said the state government was ready to provide assistance to the owners of the five business premises, including support for rebuilding efforts. Chow said the Penang Fire and Rescue Department, assisted by the Volunteer Fire Brigade, had brought the fire under control, while efforts to remove the timber stacks continued after traces of the fire were detected in the wooden structures.

items.title: 'Enough fighting,' Sanusi tells off 'stubborn' Perlis PN leaders
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Noor has reminded Perlis Perikatan Nasional leaders to stop bickering and avoid repeating the conflicts that have previously plagued the coalition in the state. Sanusi, who is also Pas election director, said the same reminder had been issued before, but the infighting had instead become worse. It was previously reported that the Perlis Pas Youth wing had urged the Pas and PN leadership to consider stern action against Perlis Menteri Besar Abu Bakar Hamzah, who was alleged to be increasingly tarnishing the image of PN and Pas in the state .

items.title: ‘If Langkawi too small’: Defence minister says LIMA may need alternative venue
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 5 — The proposal to explore an alternative venue for the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA) in the future is aimed at keeping the event competitive amid growing competition among defence exhibitions in the region. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said continuous improvements to LIMA, particularly in terms of venue size and facilities, were necessary, especially as more neighbouring countries were also organising similar exhibitions. Mohamed Khaled said the government should consider developments in the defence exhibition industry in neighbouring countries, which now offer more extensive facilities and exhibition space.

items.title: Man arrested with RM1.46mil worth of vape pods in Tumpat
items.summary: TUMPAT: A man was arrested after being found in possession of more than 14,600 vape pods worth RM1.46 million in an operation at Kampung Kutan, Pasir Pekan, here, last night. He said, acting on public tip-offs, a team stopped the 22-year-old suspect in front of a mosque in Pengkalan Kubor. "The vape pods were then smuggled into Thailand through an illegal jetty in Pengkalan Kubor," he said.

items.title: Haze: Govt ready to declare emergency if API exceeds 400
items.summary: Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said three areas, which are Kuching, Kota Samarahan, and Sri Aman have recorded very unhealthy air quality levels. He said the government will focus cloud seeding operations on these three areas where the API exceeds 400. "Out of 68 air pollution monitoring stations, only three recorded very unhealthy air levels.

items.title: Pas will not surrender potential winning seats, says Sanusi
items.summary: KOTA BHARU: Pas will not surrender seats identified as potential wins to any party for the 16th General Election (GE16). Pas central election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said these winnable seats will be identified by the party's central and state election machinery. We must not give away those seats to anyone.

items.title: Government ready to declare emergency if API exceeds 400, says Arthur Kurup
items.summary: KUALA BERANG, Sept 5 — The government is ready to propose declaring an emergency for any area that records an Air Pollution Index (API) reading of more than 400, in line with the standard operating procedure for haze management in the country. Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the measure could be considered if the API reading was at a very dangerous level, as happened in Serian, Sarawak which recorded a reading of more than 500, leading to the declaration of an emergency. Arthur said so far only three of the 68 API monitoring stations nationwide had recorded very unhealthy readings, namely in Kuching, Samarahan and Sri Aman in Sarawak, while Serian recorded readings at a dangerous level.

items.title: Tok Mat : DNA samples of 55 Malaysians' next of kin ready for Nepal matching
items.summary: SEREMBAN: DNA samples from the next of kin of 55 Malaysians previously reported as unreachable following devastating floods in Nepal have been obtained, completing the required sample collection. Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the samples would be sent to Nepal soon for DNA matching. "We have just completed collecting DNA samples from all the victims' immediate family members, and the samples will be sent to Nepal for matching.

items.title: ‘Not just Kota Kinabalu’: MOH targets Sandakan, Tawau clusters in Sabah specialist expansion
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 5 — The Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) will begin placing resident specialists in several hospitals in Sabah such as Kota Marudu and Beaufort as a measure to overcome the shortage of specialists in the state. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the effort also complements the ministry’s initiative to move specialist rotation to rural areas in Sabah. Dr Dzulkefly said MOH has also aggressively expanded the Hospital Services Outsourcing Programme initiative to the private sector to address congestion in public hospital lobbies and wards.

items.title: Don't rush GE16 seat talks, says Johari
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Discussions regarding seat allocations between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) for the 16th General Election (GE16) should be left to the top leaders of both coalitions, says Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. The Umno vice-president said that every political party naturally seeks to defend the seats it won in the previous election and seat allocations should not complicate efforts to build an understanding between BN and PN. "Pas wants to defend its seats, and Umno also wants to defend the seats it won.

items.title: From completion to excellence
items.summary: When teams experience this success, something important often happens beyond the project itself: motivation grows, confidence strengthens and a desire for excellence begins to take root. Every project presents challenges. Success also creates confidence.

items.title: Lima: Alternative venues being explored amid rising regional competition — Khaled
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: The proposal to explore an alternative venue for the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (Lima) in the future is aimed at keeping the event competitive amid growing competition among defence exhibitions in the region. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said continuous improvements to Lima, particularly in terms of venue size and facilities, were necessary, especially as more neighbouring countries were also organising similar exhibitions. Mohamed Khaled said the government should consider developments in the defence exhibition industry in neighbouring countries, which now offer more extensive facilities and exhibition space.

items.title: Nepal Floods: Prioritise mental health support for families of missing Malaysians
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Wisma Putra has been called on to act swiftly and prioritise mental health support for families of Malaysians still missing following the Nepal disaster. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (Masfih) member Dr R. Manivannan said families should not have to wait days for psychological support while facing prolonged uncertainty over their loved ones. Manivannan said such delays could discourage other affected families from seeking help.

items.title: Serian town unusually quiet amid thick haze and emergency declaration
items.summary: SERIAN, Sept 5 — The usually vibrant streets of Serian town, typically bustling with weekend crowds, appeared unusually quiet today, amidst the ongoing haze and the declaration of an emergency in the area. A Bernama check around the town found that health concerns had disrupted daily activities. However, the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed a downward trend from the hazardous levels above 500 recorded the day before.

items.title: Thai DPM Sihasak to undertake two‑day working visit to Malaysia from Sept 6
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sihasak Phuangketkeow, is scheduled to pay a two-day working visit to Malaysia from Sunday to September 7, according to the PR Thai Government. In its Facebook post on Friday, it noted that the visit would follow up on and advance the issues discussed by the leaders of the two countries during the Thai Prime Minister’s official visit to Malaysia on July 9 to 10. The delegation is scheduled to meet Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan to discuss border security and joint development of border areas.

items.title: Masseuse dies after falling from fourth-floor shoplot while fleeing inspection
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A 36-year-old foreign masseuse died after falling from the fourth floor of a shoplot in Bandar Baru Permas Jaya, Masai, while allegedly trying to flee an enforcement inspection two days ago. Johor Baru Selatan deputy police chief Superintendent Ng Swie Chait said police received a report on the incident at 3.48pm. "Initial investigations found that the woman allegedly fell from the fourth floor while trying to escape during an inspection by the Johor Baru City Council (MBJB) at the premises where she worked.

items.title: Zambry: Malaysia Higher Education Plan 2026-2035 aims to shape students with strong values alongside academic excellence
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 5 — The Malaysia Higher Education Plan (RPTM) 2026–2035 is focused on developing students who are not only academically competent but also grounded in strong values and good character. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the goal of education is not merely to produce knowledgeable and skilled graduates, but to shape better individuals who are capable of navigating a changing world and the demands of the job market. “The purpose of education is to make us better people.

items.title: Pas-Umno cooperation should continue until GE16, says Mubarak chief
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The growing cooperation between Pas and Umno is a positive development that should be sustained at least until the 16th General Election (GE16). Kelantan Council of Former Elected Representatives (Mubarak) president Datuk Mohd Rozali Isohak said such cooperation should have taken place long ago. Pas and Umno have been moving towards renewed political cooperation ahead of GE16.

items.title: Workplaces in Serian may operate during haze emergency with health precautions, says SDMC
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Government, private offices and other workplaces affected by the haze emergency in Serian, including industries, plantations, construction sites and quarries may continue their operations but must take health precautionary measures. Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas, who is also state Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman, said the committee is closely monitoring the haze situation across Sarawak, particularly the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in Serian. “SDMC is currently monitoring the API level in Serian within these three days in anticipation for any fluctuation of the API level, should it increase to a level above 500.

items.title: Nadma sends 11‑member SMART team to Nepal for flood and landslide SAR
items.summary: SUBANG, Sept 5 — Eleven personnel and officers from the Special Malaysian Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) departed for Nepal this morning to assist search and rescue (SAR) operations in areas affected by floods and landslides. National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the team is led by commander Abdul Manaf Che Isa, with the mission expected to last 10 days. Eleven members of the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) depart for Nepal from Subang Air Base September 5, 2026.

items.title: Air Kelantan: Pipe leak cuts water supply in Machang, Pasir Puteh and Kota Bharu Selatan, affecting 34,000 accounts
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 5 — Production capacity at the Merbau Chondong Water Treatment Plant (WTP) in Machang has dropped by almost half following a leak in a 1,000-millimetre Glass-Fibre Reinforced Plastic (GRP) raw water pipe, said Air Kelantan Sdn Bhd (AKSB). In a statement today, AKSB said the incident had disrupted water supply in three districts, namely Machang, parts of Pasir Puteh and Kota Bharu Selatan, affecting almost 34,000 consumer accounts. AKSB is also mobilising water tankers to assist affected consumers, while water operators from other states have also agreed to send tankers to the affected areas,” AKSB said.

items.title: PM to deliver closing address and present Agro Awards at MAHA 2026 tomorrow
items.summary: SERDANG, Sept 5 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to officiate the closing ceremony of the Malaysia Agriculture, Horticulture and Agro-Tourism Exhibition (MAHA 2026) at the Malaysia Agro Exposition Park (MAEPS), here tomorrow. Based on the programme, Anwar is scheduled to arrive at 10.30 am before delivering the Closing Address at Hall D2 and performing the Closing Gimmick of MAHA 2026. Also scheduled to be present are the two Deputy Prime Ministers and Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.

items.title: Sydney sweats in spring hot spell, faces 'extreme' bushfire risk
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australia's most populous city Sydney baked in a burst of sweltering spring heat on Saturday, raising the risk of bushfires and prompting authorities to issue a ban on lighting fires. "Fresh to strong and gusty northwesterly winds developing during the morning, combined with dry, unseasonably warm conditions, will result in elevated fire dangers across the Greater Sydney Region today," the forecaster said. State fire authorities issued a total fire ban for Sydney, where they rated fire risk as "extreme", the second-highest danger rating.

items.title: Pas hopes no 'fire-starters' will derail unity of ummah
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Pas is hoping there will be no more "fire-starters" burning bridges or "invisible hands" working to derail its agenda of ummah (Muslim community) unity. Pas Indera Mahkota delegate Nasrudin Hassan Tantawi said unity did not mean sacrificing principles, but rather strengthening the Muslim community, managing differences with decorum and prioritising the interests of Islam. "Ummah unity is not merely a political strategy.

items.title: Anak Krakatau continues to erupt, lava fountains reported
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano, located in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra, continued to erupt on Saturday morning, with booming and rumbling sounds heard from an observation post as authorities reported lava-fountaining activity. National Disaster Mitigation Agency (BNPB) Disaster Data, Information and Communication Centre Acting Head Berton Panjaitan said the eruption began at 11.07pm local time on Friday and continued throughout the observation period from midnight to 6am on Saturday. Anak Krakatau, administratively located in South Lampung regency, Lampung province, remains at Level III, or Siaga (Alert), with authorities maintaining a three-kilometre exclusion zone around its active crater.

items.title: Pas at 75: Quiet celebration, louder political message
items.summary: Instead, the diamond jubilee was observed simply, reflecting the character the party has sought to project throughout its political journey — grassroots support, modesty and religious identity. That simplicity takes on added meaning as Pas enters a potentially consequential period in its political history. Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man said the party would not sacrifice its principles simply to win power or reach Putrajaya.

items.title: Hot-air balloon basket kills German tourist in Switzerland
items.summary: GENEVA: An 86-year-old German man died after being struck by the basket of a hot-air balloon on a meadow in Switzerland near Lake Constance, canton Thurgau police said on Friday, reported German news agency dpa. He had been part of a group, some of whom intended to take part in the balloon flight, a police spokesman told dpa. The balloon was due to take off from a meadow near Salen-Reutenen, around 20 kilometres west of the city of Konstanz.

items.title: MOH: Malaysia to lead 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting in Kuala Lumpur from Sept 7-11
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Malaysia will chair the 17th Asean Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM), which begins September 7 in the capital, the Ministry of Health (MOH) announced. Organised by the MOH, the conference reflects the ministry’s pivotal role as a leader in regional health diplomacy, tasked with coordinating policy directions, digital health innovation and health crisis preparedness at the Asean level. Held biennially, the AHMM is the primary platform for Asean Health Ministers to discuss regional health issues and strengthen collaboration and coordination across the health sector.

items.title: PIL2A first phase reaches 29.85pct completion, paving way to Silicon Island
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The first phase of the Pan Island Link 2A (PIL2A) has reached 29.85 per cent completion, with work progressing 0.42 per cent ahead of schedule. The RM420 million first phase involves a 1.5km road and marine bridge linking an interchange at Jalan Permatang Damar Laut directly to Silicon Island. State Infrastructure and Transport Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the progress reflected the commitment of the Penang government, project developer and contractors to ensuring smooth project implementation.

items.title: Public briefing on Sarawak electoral boundary review set for Sept 8 in Kuching
items.summary: ROSE president Geoffrey Tang said the session would feature EC commissioner Mohd Faisal Syam Abdul Hazis, who would be accompanied by EC Sarawak director Abang Noraffian Abang Ibrahim. “Electoral boundary review is an important process that has a direct impact on how people are represented in the electoral system,” he said in a statement. he said.

items.title: Nepal floods: 55 Malaysians still uncontactable after 10 days
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Ten days after devastating floods struck the Nepal-China border region, the fate of 55 Malaysians who remain unreachable is still unknown, according to Wisma Putra. "The Malaysian Embassy in Beijing remains in contact with Chinese authorities, while the ministry is also engaging the Chinese Embassy in Kuala Lumpur for official clarification," it said. Malaysia has also expressed its readiness to provide appropriate search-and-rescue expertise if requested by Chinese authorities.

items.title: PSM urges halt to PPR Taman Manggis evictions as housing board defends enforcement
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Parti Sosialis Malaysia (PSM) has urged Penang authorities to halt evictions at PPR Taman Manggis, while the Penang Housing Board defended the action. PSM Penang said five units at the People's Housing Programme (PPR) Taman Manggis were locked by authorities on Sept 3, with several more residents allegedly facing eviction. PSM Penang spokesman Choo Chon Kai said residents deemed to have lost their eligibility were being evicted without being offered permanent housing alternatives.

items.title: Understand and follow guidelines before flying Jalur Gemilang, including AI‑generated images, says national unity minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Malaysians are urged to exercise greater care and always refer to the proper guidelines when installing and displaying the Jalur Gemilang. National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said the Jalur Gemilang was a symbol of national sovereignty, dignity and unity that all Malaysians, regardless of race, religion or political affiliation, must respect. Aaron said the National Unity Ministry, through the Kawasan Rukun Tetangga (KRT) and Rukun Negara Secretariat, would step up efforts to raise public awareness of the correct procedures for installing and displaying the Jalur Gemilang.

items.title: Smart's main focus in Nepal is locating missing Malaysians
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Malaysia's Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (Smart) is expected to remain in Nepal for seven to 10 days to assist in the humanitarian mission following devastating floods. National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the 11 officers and personnel deployed had various specialised skills, including search and rescue (SAR), drone operations, logistics, communications and technical support. They are expected to arrive at 11am Nepal time (1pm Malaysian time).

items.title: Perak exco hopes Budget 2027 will prioritise welfare of older rural residents
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 5 — The Perak state government hopes Budget 2027 will give special attention to the welfare of senior citizens in rural areas, covering housing, basic amenities, mobility as well as digital access. State Rural Development, Plantation, Agriculture and Food Industry Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Zolkafly Harun said the attention was important with the increasing elderly population in the state, as well as the migration of young people to urban areas, which resulted in some senior citizens in rural areas, especially those living alone, to face limited access to support facilities. He also drew attention to housing, stressing that serious attention was needed as there were still low-income (B40) groups in rural areas living in houses that were too dilapidated and no longer economically viable to repair.

items.title: Chew Jetty unaffected by fire 20m away, says Penang CM
items.summary: "Chew Jetty is not affected and is not involved in this fire. The fire site is about 20 metres from Chew Jetty," Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said when visiting the site this morning. Chow said the fire, reported about 1am, involved six premises comprising workshops, a carpentry business and other businesses.

items.title: Police detain four in separate cable theft cases in Kampar and Kuala Kangsar
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 5 — Police detained four local men early yesterday morning in connection with two separate cable theft cases in Kampar and Kuala Kangsar. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the first arrest in Kampar was made at about 4.30 am when a Malim Nawar Police Station patrol team spotted two men, aged 42 and 46, acting suspiciously at the Muniswarar Temple in Bata Malim Nawar. He said the inspection resulted in the seizure of two cable cutters and five rolls of cable, which Telekom Malaysia (TM) technicians later confirmed belonged to the company.

items.title: "I stayed silent out of fear": Student recounts obscene conversation with e-hailing driver
items.summary: Putery, from Seremban, Negri Sembilan, said she took a bus to Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday and was supposed to arrive at the terminal at 9pm. Putery contacted the driver after arriving at the terminal. Putery said the driver continued talking about sex throughout the journey.

items.title: Serian haze eases slightly, but API remains hazardous at 390 at 7am; Kuching, Tebedu, Lundu remain at very unhealthy levels
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Air quality in Serian improved slightly, with its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading dropping to 390 by 7am today from 498, which was categorised as very hazardous at 8pm yesterday. Limbang’s air quality deteriorated, with its API reading soaring to 155, an unhealthy level, from a moderate reading of 96 at 8pm. The API reading in Kapit also climbed into the unhealthy zone, reaching 122 from a moderate reading of 93 at 8pm.

items.title: Police detain 11 over machete attack in Ipoh that left victim seriously injured
items.summary: Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the 26-year-old victim was approached by five men travelling in two cars at about 10.30 am, who then chased and assaulted him. Mohd Alwi said members of the public later came to the victim’s aid before taking him to hospital for treatment. Mohd Alwi said all those arrested, aged between 22 and 41, had previous criminal records involving drug offences and violent crimes.

items.title: National Resilience College to nurture leaders for Malaysia’s evolving security landscape, says Khaled Nordin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — The National Resilience College (NRC) needs to continue to be strengthened as a credible institution in shaping leadership capable of navigating the country’s increasingly complex security and defence landscape. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the college is an important platform in enhancing understanding of national security and defence among senior leaders in the defence, security and civil sectors. Mohamed Khaled said NRC is an institution under the National Defence Studies Centre (Puspahanas), which plays a role in developing strategic leadership.

items.title: Sungai Besi Highway’s 400m lane‑widening project completed, opens to traffic Monday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — The 400-metre widening project near the Seri Kembangan Interchange (southbound) on the Sungai Besi Highway (Besraya) is now fully completed and will be opened to traffic starting this Monday. As a result, users of the Besraya Highway from Kuala Lumpur to Balakong and Putrajaya can now enjoy a more comfortable journey. Besraya (M) Sdn Bhd in a statement announced that the RM5.22 million project was implemented with the support of the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) involving the route from KM4.2 to KM3.8 of the Besraya Highway (southbound).

items.title: Early-morning fire destroys five business premises at Penang’s Chew Jetty heritage area
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 5 — Five business premises at the iconic Chew Jetty heritage area here were destroyed in a fire that broke out early this morning. “The fire involved five premises, including a car workshop, welding shop and timber factory. Everything was destroyed,” he said.

items.title: KL DOE flags three fake govt order scams to warn vendors and protect procurement integrity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — The Kuala Lumpur Federal Territory Department of Environment (JAS WPKL) has detected at least three attempted scams using fake government order documents that misused the name, logo, and identities of several department officers. She noted that the company received a suspicious government order document featuring the JAS logo on the cover, with a total order value of RM26,000. “These fake government order documents were found to have misused the names of several JAS Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur officers,” she said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: Immigration Dept reviewing SOP compliance as internal probe into fatal Maju junction crash continues
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 5 — The Immigration Department is still conducting an internal investigation into safety and standard operating procedures (SOP) relating to the operating of department vehicles following a recent fatal crash along Jalan Sultan Ismail in Kuala Lumpur. If there are violations or SOPs that need improvement, we will take action to improve so that such incidents don’t recur,” he said when asked about developments on the fatal crash at a media conference after a department operation here today The crash involving an empty department Black Maria lorry on October 19 occurred when it ran a red light with its beacon and siren activated and rammed a Proton Saga, skidded and hit a family of four, killed three and severely injuring another. The driver is currently facing five charges in relation to the crash after he was charged at the Kuala Lumpur Magistrate’s Court the following day.

items.title: Air Itam armed brawl: Police make 10 more arrests after raids in Penang and Selangor
items.summary: Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the latest arrests were made following several raids conducted in Penang and Selangor after the initial detention of 13 suspects. “The latest arrests involved local men aged between 19 and 56, following several operations conducted by police to assist investigations into the case,” he said in a statement last night. Lim said investigations found that the incident, which occurred at about 2.45am outside SJK(C) Kong Min Branch Two, Ayer Itam, involved three local men aged between 17 and 25.

items.title: Nepal clears SMART deployment as families of missing Malaysians await news
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Families of Malaysins who went missing following the recent flash floods in Nepal are hopeful for some news from the field following the Nepali government’s approval of the deployment of the Special Malaysian Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) from today. Muhammad Firas Shah Shabuddin, the youngest child of Shabuddin Mun, one of 10 Malaysians from Team Loe heading to Everest Base Camp (EBC), expressed relief about the latest development. The 11-member strong SMART team is expected to be deployed tomorrow and will assist search efforts by local Nepali authorities, especially in areas requiring technical expertise and specific operational capabilities.

items.title: Fadhlina calls on parents and schools to follow official haze updates as Sarawak shuts 647 schools
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has urged parents and school communities to follow the official channels of the Sarawak State Education Department (JPN) for updates and the latest announcements regarding the haze situation in the state. Through a Facebook post last night, she said that the health and safety of children must be prioritised, and Sarawak JPN will continue to monitor the situation from time to time. “Take care of your health and reduce outdoor activities during this haze condition.
